ai.definition: DeepSeek Platform is a software solution that leverages deep learning techniques to process natural language and extract meaningful insights from unstructured text data.
ai.howItWorks: The platform uses neural networks to analyze large volumes of textual information, identifying patterns, relationships, and contextual meanings. It involves preprocessing the text data, training models on labeled datasets, and fine-tuning these models for specific tasks such as sentiment analysis, entity recognition, or topic modeling.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenge of extracting valuable insights from vast amounts of unstructured textual data, which is difficult to process using traditional rule-based methods.
ai.manufacturing: The platform is software-based and does not involve physical manufacturing processes. It requires computational resources for training models but operates on existing hardware infrastructure.
ai.buildProcess: Development involves gathering and labeling datasets, designing neural network architectures, training the models, and integrating them into a user-friendly interface. Continuous updates are necessary to adapt to evolving language patterns and requirements.
ai.costDrivers: Costs include data acquisition and annotation, computational resources for model training, ongoing maintenance, and software development efforts.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The platform is currently in use by various enterprises but has potential for broader adoption across industries as NLP technologies continue to advance.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary depending on the industry and region. Privacy laws, data protection regulations, and ethical guidelines are relevant considerations.
ai.risks: Risks include data privacy concerns, model bias, and the need for continuous updates to stay current with language changes and technological advancements.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the market demand for NLP solutions and the ability to scale operations efficiently. The platform can generate revenue through licensing fees, subscription models, or as a service offering.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may focus on improving model accuracy, reducing training time, expanding language support, and integrating multimodal data sources.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to computational requirements for model training but not significant in operational use.

glossary.def: A subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex patterns and features from data.
The field of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language.

subsystems.name: Data and tokeniser
subsystems.role: turns raw text into the token IDs the model actually learns from.
parts: byte-level tokeniser with a large vocabulary

subsystems.name: Sparse mixture-of-experts layers
subsystems.role: replaces the single dense feed-forward block in each layer with many expert blocks, of which only a few fire per token.

subsystems.name: Attention with compressed cache
subsystems.role: lets every token attend to earlier ones without storing a full key/value table for each head.

subsystems.name: Training stack
subsystems.role: runs pretraining and fine-tuning across thousands of accelerators.

subsystems.name: Post-training for reasoning
subsystems.role: teaches the model to work through problems step by step rather than answer immediately.

subsystems.name: Inference and serving layer
subsystems.role: makes a very large model cheap enough to answer queries.

subsystems.name: Distillation pipeline
subsystems.role: copies the large model's behaviour into small dense models that run locally.

buildSteps.title: Collect and clean the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Crawl text and code, strip boilerplate, remove duplicates and filter for quality and safety — this shapes the model more than any later step.

buildSteps.title: Design the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Choose layer count, hidden width, the number of experts per layer and how many are active per token, balancing quality against inference cost.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain on a large cluster
buildSteps.detail: Run next-token prediction for weeks on thousands of accelerators, using low-precision arithmetic and parallelism across chips to fit the model in memory.

buildSteps.title: Supervised fine-tuning
buildSteps.detail: Train on curated question–answer pairs so the raw text predictor becomes a usable assistant.

buildSteps.title: Reinforcement learning for reasoning
buildSteps.detail: Sample many answers per problem, score them against checkable answers (maths, code), and update the model toward the patterns that succeeded.

buildSteps.title: Distil into smaller models
buildSteps.detail: Use the large model to generate training data for compact versions that fit on a single server or a laptop.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and red-team
buildSteps.detail: Test accuracy, reasoning, bias and safety; fix failure modes before release.

buildSteps.title: Serve and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Quantise, batch and cache for cheap inference, publish weights, and feed production failures back into the next training round.

prerequisites.why: the attention-and-feed-forward block is the base every modern language model is built from.
training a model of this size needs many thousands of high-bandwidth GPUs and fast interconnects.
8-bit and lower arithmetic cuts memory and time without wrecking accuracy.

prerequisites.tech: Scalable reinforcement learning for language models
prerequisites.why: RL on verifiable tasks works well for maths and code but is harder to extend to open-ended domains.
serving reasoning models at scale is expensive because they emit many tokens per query.

pathway.milestone: open-weight mixture-of-experts models with exposed reasoning traces
pathway.unlocks: frontier-class capability that anyone can download, fine-tune or self-host.

pathway.milestone: cheaper long-chain reasoning through better caching, distillation and quantisation
pathway.unlocks: reasoning models affordable at high query volumes and on local hardware.

pathway.milestone: reliable tool use and agentic loops
pathway.unlocks: models that plan, call software and verify their own results rather than only answering.

pathway.milestone: reinforcement learning extended to domains without a checkable answer
pathway.unlocks: steady improvement in research, engineering and medicine rather than just maths and code.

pathway.milestone: multimodal and on-device versions of the same stack
pathway.unlocks: private, low-latency assistance without sending data to a data centre.
